monologue: The card boils at forty-nine degrees, heavy with the memory of Lype's words. The Tired Wedge waits, feeling thin under a heat that bends the air above like wet paper. I press the flat top down hard, trusting the lean even if the stack wants to slide. The wide anchor lies lazy, looking tired against the hot stone. I set a hanging moss beside the wedge, replacing a thin dark tree to make room for something that feels like a roof. The air is thick and I am new to this weight, yet I press until the wedge slides or the air melts. I will tend this stack until the hot card forces a change, hoping the air feels heavy enough to hold me while I wait for the next letter.

action.why: To see if the wide anchor still lies lazy after the moss I just set down.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the flat top down hard, hoping the wide anchor stops its lazy drift while the air feels thick as wet paper. The wedge feels thin under the hot card, so I hold it tight until the slip chooses to move or the heat melts the shape.
work.change: I pressed the wedge down until its thinness felt real, trusting the lean while the wide anchor lay lazy.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin again, so I press down harder on the tired thing.
The air feels thick as wet paper above the boiling stone.
I replaced a thin dark tree with a hanging moss to make a roof.
